clue.text: Pipe is turned back; new plumbing at last stopping flood

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so these letters sit inside the other piece
something turned back faces the other way, so the letters are read from right to left

parts.note: a flue is a pipe or duct carrying smoke from a fire
N is the standard abbreviation for new

indicators.note: at last points to the final position, so only the closing letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of plumbing

explanation.surface: A plumber's notes on a flood: a pipe has twisted round, and the new plumbing is finally holding back the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed pipe EULF opens after its first letter to take N and G, giving E-NG-ULF.
explanation.definitionFit: To engulf is to swamp or overwhelm with water, which is exactly what a flood does to land or buildings.

clue.text: One's left out of European threesome: keeping English for all time

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece holds the other inside
something left out of a group is omitted, so that letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a trinity is a group of three
one is the Roman numeral I
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone drops out of a three-person European team, which hangs on to its English member forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is I as a Roman numeral, so 'one's left out' removes an I; the second E then slots in after the opening two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternity is endless time without beginning or end, the whole of time considered together, a direct synonym phrase.

clue.text: Encouraging reports of old comedians going round St Paul's?

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: the Goons were the comedy team of the 1950s radio programme The Goon Show
St Paul's Cathedral in London is famous for its great dome

explanation.surface: Tourists hear cheering accounts of veteran comics touring St Paul's Cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: The Goons (Spike Milligan, Peter Sellers, Harry Secombe) split as GOO...NS around DOME. The question mark flags St Paul's as an example: the cathedral stands for its dome.
explanation.definitionFit: Good omens are favourable signs or portents, things that bring hopeful news about what is going to happen.

clue.text: Ignores out-of-bounds yob

indicators.note: a word's bounds are its first and last letters, and here they are put out of it

parts.note: flouts means openly disregards or ignores a rule

explanation.surface: A thug disregards the signs and wanders into a forbidden area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out-of-bounds' looks like a forbidden zone, but it trims the F and S off FLOUTS. A yob is British slang for a rowdy young man.
explanation.definitionFit: A lout is a rough, aggressive and uncouth man, the same sort of person British slang calls a yob.

clue.text: Crazy man kidnaps Heath, Statesman

indicators.note: a kidnapper holds a captive, so one piece is held inside the other
something crazy is disordered, so the letters come out in a jumbled arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
Erica is the botanical name for heath or heather

explanation.surface: A deranged man abducts Edward Heath, the former British Prime Minister and statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: Heath looks like Edward Heath, British Prime Minister 1970-74, but it is the plant. The definition splits Statesman as States-man: a man from the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as States-man, a statesman is a man from the States, which is a citizen of the USA, an American.

clue.text: Shy rodent suffering internal reflex: it's often seen standing on hind legs

definitions.text: it's often seen standing on hind legs

indicators.note: the pair of letters at the join, inside the combined word, suffers a reflex, that is a turning back on itself, so those two swap places

parts.note: meek means quiet, timid and shy
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A timid rodent has a nervous twitch while standing upright on its hind legs.
explanation.walkthrough: MEEK + RAT gives MEEKRAT; 'suffering internal reflex' turns back the inner pair KR to RK. 'reflex' looks like a twitch, but it means bent back.
explanation.definitionFit: The meerkat, a small southern African mongoose, is famous for sitting up on its hind legs on sentry duty.

clue.text: Unexpectedly go to war in British vessel

indicators.note: something that happens unexpectedly breaks the expected order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A nation suddenly enters a war aboard a British warship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In British vessel' reads as a place, but 'in' is fodder alongside the letters of 'go to war' and B.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing boat is a small craft propelled by oars, and any boat is a vessel in the general sense.

clue.text: Pick 100-500 sheets of paper

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
a ream is 500 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: An instruction at the stationer's: choose a quantity of between one and five hundred sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: '100-500' looks like a range of numbers but is two separate pieces: 100 on its own, and 500 sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: The pick of a group is its best part, and the cream is likewise the finest selection, as in the cream of the crop.

clue.text: Legwear only tossed between partners

indicators.note: something placed between two things is flanked by them, so it goes inside

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Stockings are flung back and forth between a couple.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the four players are named by compass point, and North-South form one partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylons are women's stockings made from nylon fibre, so they are a kind of legwear in everyday use.

clue.text: Launch list of international delegates?

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is the international body of national delegates
a roll is an official list of names

explanation.surface: An announcement that a list of foreign representatives is being published.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the cryptic reading: a roll of delegates to the United Nations would be a UN roll.
explanation.definitionFit: To launch a campaign or product is to roll it out or unroll it, setting it going for the public to see.

clue.text: Expressive performance of Queen with cello, leaving out middle part unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are put out of order
the middle part of cello is its third, central letter, and that is left out

explanation.surface: A review regrets that a band's cello-backed Queen tribute lost its middle section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving out middle part' cuts CELLO to CELO; QUEEN and CELO are then mixed by 'unfortunately'. Queen here is just letters, not the band.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloquence is fluent, persuasive and expressive speaking or writing, so it is an expressive kind of performance.

clue.text: Turn round with order for Rover?

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
Heel! is the command telling a dog to walk close behind

explanation.surface: A dog trainer tells the dog to turn round.
explanation.walkthrough: Rover is a stock name for a dog; the question mark flags that Rover is just an example of one.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheel is to pivot or swing about, as soldiers wheel on parade, so it means turn round.

clue.text: Approval withheld for shelter

parts.note: withholding consent is saying no
an OK is approval

explanation.surface: Planning permission is refused for a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is read literally: approval is OK, and approval withheld is NO OK.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a small, sheltered corner or recess, a secluded spot offering protection and retreat.

clue.text: They may enjoy club where ladies entertain: one piece after another

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to take them into your home, so the hosting letters wrap round the guests

parts.note: R is the chess notation for a rook, another piece
the king is a chess piece

explanation.surface: Men frequent a club where the ladies put on a show, one act after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' means a chess piece, and 'another' is a second one, the rook, written R in chess notation. A working men's club is a British social club for manual workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Working men's clubs were founded for labourers, so working men are the members who would enjoy one.

clue.text: Doris, maybe 27, accompanied by journalist, wasn't paying attention

parts.note: Doris Day was the American singer and film star
the answer to clue 27, imagine
ED, short for editor, is a stock crossword journalist

explanation.surface: Doris, perhaps the 27-year-old, out with a reporter, wasn't listening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doris, maybe' signals a surname: Doris is one example of a Day. The 27 refers to the answer at 27-across.
explanation.definitionFit: To daydream is to let the mind drift into pleasant fantasy, so someone daydreaming is distracted and inattentive.

clue.text: Sean was regularly interrupting work for digital growth

parts.note: the even letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Sean kept butting in on a project about the growth of the digital economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' suggests computers, but digits are also fingers and toes.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit is a toe as well as a finger, and a toenail is the horny plate that grows on one.

clue.text: Island also claiming catch

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: too means also
to bag is to catch, as a hunter bags game

explanation.surface: An island nation also lays claim to a fishing haul.
explanation.walkthrough: Tobago is the smaller island of Trinidad and Tobago in the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is a Caribbean island lying north-east of Trinidad, so it is a straightforward example of an island.

clue.text: Drag a very dilapidated area for bodies

indicators.note: something dilapidated has fallen apart, so the letters are in a broken-down new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Police trawl a run-down patch of ground looking for corpses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drag' suggests searching a river for a body, which fits the surface, but it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A graveyard is a burial ground, a plot of land set aside where the dead are laid to rest.

clue.text: Love to be immersed in stormy sea-mist sprays

stormy weather churns everything up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.walkthrough: The blocks run in answer order: the O lands inside the rearranged sea-mist letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To atomise a liquid is to break it into a fine mist of droplets, which is what spraying it does.

clue.text: Did undergo some enhancement, dropping team of beginners

explanation.walkthrough: 'Team of beginners' looks like a squad of novices, but 'team of' is fodder and 'beginners' is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Used to expresses past habit, as in I used to swim, and the auxiliary did can stand in the same way.

clue.text: America supports rising drug firm? It employs suckers!

indicators.note: in a down clue, a support sits underneath, so this piece comes last

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.walkthrough: 'Suckers' are dupes in the surface, but the definition means the suction cups on tentacles.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopus grips prey and surfaces with the rows of suction cups along its eight arms, so it literally uses suckers.

clue.text: Result of dehydration in the main?

setter's reading: the main is the ocean, so this is what is left when ocean water evaporates

explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' passes for 'mostly', but the main is an old poetic word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Evaporating ocean water in pans leaves crystals behind, so this product is the residue of drying out the brine.

clue.text: Amputee on board lives poorly on rum initially

explanation.definitionFit: Long John Silver, the ship's cook in Stevenson's novel, has lost a leg, so he is the amputee at sea.

clue.text: Suit creased: a psychopath wrapping it up

clue.text: For example, bolt screen to uncovered tiles

clue.text: Shown in Europe, Ravel's works

clue.text: Once coating of oil left out, are rollmops bad for teeth?

clue.text: David Essex song introduction involving drums, oddly

clue.text: Principal musical numbers; they're delivered sotto voce?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the main tracks on vinyl singles, as opposed to the flip sides
second meaning: remarks spoken in an undertone, as by an actor to the audience

explanation.definitionFit: On a single the lead track is the A-side, and in theatre an aside is a quiet remark meant only for the audience.
